setup.title: OWA Mail MCP setup
setup.s1_lead: The same details you use to sign in to your company's web mail (OWA). The password is kept in the system keychain, not in a file.
setup.server_hint: Your web mail address: mail.company.com, https://owa.company.com or https://outlook.company.com/owa
setup.username_hint: If your company uses Windows sign-in (single sign-on), enter DOMAIN\login.
setup.password_placeholder_stored: saved — leave empty to keep it
setup.password_stored_hint: The password is already saved in the keychain.
setup.proxy_hint: Only needed if your browser reaches the mail server through a proxy that the system settings don't show (for example, one set by a PAC script). The system proxy is picked up automatically.
setup.s2_lead: The assistant reads mail: checks new messages, searches, reads conversations and looks people up in the address book.
setup.allow_send_hint: Each message opens in a separate browser window: you see the recipients (external ones highlighted), the subject and the text, and you click Send, Edit or Don't send yourself. Nothing goes out without your click.
setup.domains_hint: Your own email domain is included automatically; add other company domains here.
setup.timeout: How long to wait for confirmation, seconds
setup.timeout_hint: Most clients cancel a call after 60 seconds, so the default is 50.
setup.ai_warning: Subjects, texts and addresses of the messages the assistant reads are sent to the AI service you use. Make sure your company's policy allows this.
setup.s3_lead: Click Add or copy the line into your MCP client's settings. Any stdio client connects the same way: the command is the path to owa-mail-mcp, with no arguments.
setup.s3_hint: Credentials and permissions are picked up without restarting the client.
setup.journal_lead: Which tools the assistant called. Only names and times are kept, never message contents.
setup.journal_empty: Nothing yet: the assistant hasn't accessed your mail.
setup.done_text: You can close this tab. To change the settings, run owa-mail-mcp setup.
setup.cert_untrusted_title: The system doesn't trust the server's certificate
setup.cert_changed_text: You previously trusted a different certificate for this server. This may be a planned replacement, or an interception. Check the new fingerprint with your IT department.
setup.cert_untrusted_text: This happens when the certificate was issued by your company's internal certificate authority ({error}). Trust it only if you are sure this is your server.
setup.cert_declined: The certificate was not accepted; not connected.
setup.testing: Testing the connection… This can take up to a minute.
setup.legacy_title: The server uses outdated secure-connection settings
setup.legacy_text: {host}:{port} only connects with TLS settings that browsers still accept but modern OpenSSL rejects by default ({reason}). Old Exchange servers or the gateways in front of them are often set up this way. You can allow them for this server only: the certificate is still checked.
msg.enter_server_email: Enter the server address and email.
msg.email_format: The email should look like name@company.com.
msg.https_needed: HTTPS is required: the password is never sent over http.
msg.proxy_format: Enter the proxy as host:port, for example proxy.company.com:3128.
msg.auth_failed: Exchange did not accept the login or password. Check them; for Windows sign-in, the login is written as DOMAIN\login.
msg.cert_changed_retry: The server sent a different certificate than the one shown. Test the connection again.
msg.keyring_unavailable: The system keychain is not available ({error}). Set the password in the OWA_MAIL_PASSWORD environment variable in your MCP client's settings instead.
msg.written_cursor: Written to {path}. Cursor picks the server up on its own or after a restart.
msg.written_opencode: Written to {path}. Restart OpenCode; check with: opencode mcp list.
msg.written_kilo: Written to {path}. Restart Kilo Code (in VS Code: Reload Window).
msg.cli_not_found: {title}: command {cmd} not found in PATH. Copy the command and run it yourself.
msg.json_unparsable: {path} could not be read as JSON (it may contain comments). To avoid losing anything, the file was not changed: add the lines from the window manually.
msg.net_dns: The name {host} is not found in DNS. Check that the address matches the web mail address in your browser. If the VPN is on, reconnect it: sometimes the system doesn't pick up the VPN's DNS servers right away.
msg.net_proxy: The proxy {proxy} did not let the connection to {host}:{port} through: {reason}. Check the proxy address under Advanced.
msg.net_tls: The secure connection to {host}:{port} could not be established: {reason}.
msg.net_connect: Can't connect to {host}:{port} ({reason}). If your browser opens the mail anyway, it goes another way, most often through a proxy.
msg.net_proxy_hint: Look up the proxy address in your network settings or ask IT, and enter it under Advanced → Proxy.
msg.proxy_pac: The system uses automatic proxy configuration (PAC){where}, which this program doesn't read. Ask IT for the proxy address for web mail (or find it in the PAC file) and enter it under Advanced → Proxy.
msg.proxy_wpad: The system uses proxy auto-discovery (WPAD), which this program doesn't use. Enter the proxy manually under Advanced → Proxy.
diag.foreign_host: redirects to another host {host} (no password was sent there)
diag.warmed_ok: EWS works (Exchange {version}), but only on a connection that signed in to OWA first: the server drops EWS requests on a new connection. The program does this sign-in itself — update it and test the connection again.
diag.warmed_error: After signing in to OWA, EWS answers (Exchange {version}) but with an error: {error}.
diag.warmed_401: After signing in to OWA, EWS asks to sign in again and doesn't accept the login and password. Check them; for Windows sign-in, the login is written as DOMAIN\login.
diag.warmed_dropped: The server drops the connection at the EWS address even after signing in to OWA: EWS is closed to outside connections (web mail still works). Ask IT whether EWS can be opened for your account.
diag.no_answer: The server answers neither on EWS nor on OWA. Check the address and the VPN.
diag.works: EWS works (Exchange {version}) and accepted the sign-in. If the test still fails, send this diagnostic report to the developer.
diag.ews_fault: EWS answers (Exchange {version}) but returned an error: {error}.
diag.gateway: The EWS address is behind a gateway with web sign-in: the request is redirected to {where}. This happens when a company publishes only web mail (OWA) to the outside, and EWS is reachable only from the corporate network. Try with the VPN on; if that doesn't help, ask IT whether EWS (/EWS/Exchange.asmx) is available and at what address.
diag.not_found: There is nothing at /EWS/Exchange.asmx (HTTP 404): EWS is not published here or is turned off.
diag.not_found_tail: Ask IT whether EWS is available and at what address; you can enter the full address in the Server address field.
diag.forbidden: Access to EWS is forbidden (HTTP 403): the administrators have closed EWS for your account or from outside the network. Try with the VPN or ask IT.
diag.wrong_auth: EWS doesn't accept the selected sign-in method ({auth}). The server offers: {offered}. Change the Sign-in method under Advanced.
diag.bad_credentials: EWS is there but didn't accept the login and password. Check them; for Windows sign-in, the login is written as DOMAIN\login.
diag.html_page: Instead of EWS, the server returns a web page "{title}". The address seems to lead to a portal or gateway, not to Exchange. Check the address and the VPN.
diag.server_error: EWS answers with a server error (HTTP {status}). Try later or tell IT.
diag.fallback: The server doesn't answer like EWS. Details below: send them to the developer or to IT.
confirm.title: Confirm sending
confirm.sub: A message goes out only after you click Send here. The assistant can't see this page.
confirm.subject: Subject
policy.no_to: At least one recipient in To is required.
policy.too_many: Too many recipients ({n}); the limit is {limit}.
policy.bad_address: Not an email address: {list}. Only plain ASCII addresses are accepted.
policy.subject_long: The subject is longer than 255 characters.
policy.body_long: The text is longer than 100,000 characters.
policy.bidi_subject: The subject contains text-direction control characters, which make it look different from what is sent.
policy.bidi_body: The text contains text-direction control characters, which make it look different from what is sent.
policy.unknown_domain: Your own mail domain is unknown, so external recipients can't be flagged.
policy.invisible: The text contains invisible characters (zero-width spaces or similar).
policy.gone: This message is no longer waiting for confirmation.
cli.not_set_up: Not set up yet: run owa-mail-mcp setup.
cli.setup_open: open this address to set up OWA Mail MCP
cli.confirm_open: open this address to confirm the message
